name: port_terminal
_about: Build recipe for the endless mode background. Feed it to scripts/build_layer_set.py, which writes the
shipped PNGs and prints the background_layers block to paste into data/endless.json.
Layer order is DRAW ORDER, back to front. The ground comes before the container band because the band
stands on the ground and is drawn onto it, the same way a unit sprite is. Reversing those two clips the
band at the ground's far edge and reads as the containers being too small and too far away.
Sources live under build/, which is not committed. What records this work is the prompts in
art/prompts/port_terminal/, the .json sidecars gen_art.py wrote beside each generation, this file, and

layers.name: sky
layers._density: A smooth vertical wash with no hard edges anywhere, so it carries no detail worth storing at 2x. It holds no clouds: those are the drifting layer in front, and a cloud painted here would sit still while those move.

layers.name: clouds
layers._autoscroll: Pixels per second, independent of the camera. This is the only thing on screen that keeps moving while the player stands still, which is most of a match. Slow on purpose: at 6 px/s the tile takes about five minutes to come round.
layers._scroll: Touches nothing, so it is free to scroll slower than the ground. Slightly faster than the sky behind it.
layers._size: Bigger clouds make a taller drawn band, which shortens the tile at a given on-screen height -- at 0.30 this layer came out 1410px, under one viewport. Drawing it larger buys the period back and is what was wanted visually anyway.

layers.name: far
layers._base: Across the water, so it touches nothing and is free to scroll slower than the ground. Raised until its tallest masses clear the container tops: at 0.24/0.48 the whole band sat behind them and only showed through gaps, which wastes the layer.

layers.name: ground
layers._scroll: Units live in this layer's coordinate space. It must stay at 1.0 or the floor slides under them.

layers.name: mid
layers._scroll: Stands on the ground, so it shares the ground's contact line and must scroll at the ground's rate.
layers._base: 0.65 puts the stacks at the top of the belt band, which starts at 0.66.
layers._shadow: Colour sampled from the apron's own darkest 8%. Anything heavier reads as a ruled line.
